subject: Materials Science
title: Sterilization of Biomaterials
description: A 60-second lesson on Sterilization of Biomaterials.

hook.text: An implant can be perfectly biocompatible but cause deadly infection if one bacterium survives on its surface.

buildup.text: Sterilization kills all microorganisms — methods include autoclaving, gamma radiation, ethylene oxide gas, and plasma.

discovery.text: Each method affects materials differently — gamma radiation crosslinks some polymers, autoclaving melts others.

twist.text: Ethylene oxide sterilizes gently but is carcinogenic — residues must be completely removed before implantation.

climax.text: Choosing the right sterilization method is a materials decision — the wrong one destroys the device it should protect.

punchline.text: Kill bacteria without killing the material — sterilization's challenge.

quiz.question: Why can't all biomaterials be sterilized by autoclaving?
options: High heat and steam can melt or degrade some polymer materials
